newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Left seen gaining, equalling right-poll.
newsitem.headline: French Left seen gaining, equalling right-poll.

text.p: An opinion poll released on Monday showed the French left neck-and-neck with the ruling centre-right coalition and gaining ground ahead of a a two-stage parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.

The Louis Harris survey for LCI television -- the third in two days showing the left gaining ground -- found the centre-right coalition and the opposition alliance of Socialists and Communists could poll 38 percent of the votes each.

The left forged ahead in voters' hopes. Among the 1,003 voters questioned on Friday and Saturday, 45 percent said they hoped the left would win -- up from 42 the previous week -- while an unchanged 43 percent hoped for a centre-right victory.
But 63 percent believed the conservatives were more likely to win, and only 21 percent expected a left-wing triumph.
The survey put support for the ruling RPR-UDF coalition at 34 percent, three points down from the previous week, with other right-wing allies polling an additional four percent.
The Socialists stood on 27.5 percent, up from 26, with their Communist allies gaining 0.5 percent at 10.5 percent.
Ecologist groups, of which the biggest, the Greens, is an ally of the left, were unchanged on seven percent.
The far-right National Front was stable at 15 percent.
Eighteen percent of voters had no opinion. Among those who did, 30 percent said they could still change their minds.
Asked who was staging the best election campaign, 22 percent named Socialist leader Lionel Jospin and just 13 percent Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
The survey did not project a breakdown of seats in the National Assembly.
